title: Suggestions & Decisions
description: Missing facts, decision paths for the increase, lawyer-review criteria and site suggestions. Review, then choose one path per topic before anything is implemented.

rows.label: Nothing here is implemented
rows.value: This page lists missing facts, options and site improvements. Choosing or not choosing an option here changes no increase, notice or site content. Record your choice in the decision log (DL-01).
rows.notes: Read sections A to D, then decide one path per topic.

sections.title: A. Missing information: what must be found before any decision

rows.label: Are both units covered by the SF Rent Ordinance (built on or before June 13, 1979, and not otherwise exempt)?
rows.notes: Owner-supplied, unverified: built 1940, two units, both rent controlled. How to find it: look up the parcel on the Planning Property Information Map (year built, units); confirm with a Rent Board counselor (415-252-4600).

rows.label: Is each unit reported in the Rent Board Housing Inventory for the current cycle?
rows.notes: Not supplied. How to find it: the owner signs in to the Rent Board Portal and checks each unit's submission.

rows.label: Is a current rent increase license on file for each unit on the effective date of any increase?
rows.notes: Not supplied. How to find it: Portal license status, saved with the date checked. SF.gov wording on the consequence differs (F25).

rows.label: Anniversary date and every increase imposed since each tenancy began (amount, date, notice, proof of service)
rows.notes: Not supplied for either unit. How to find it: the owner's rent ledger and copies of every past notice and proof of service.

rows.label: Unit 2: current base rent
rows.notes: Owner-supplied, unverified: $3,150 per month at the June 1, 2019 lease start. Current rent not supplied. How to find it: owner's ledger; the Housing Inventory asks for base rent in $250 increments.

rows.label: Unit 1: is the April 1, 2026 occupancy a continuation of the February 1, 2025 tenancy, a new tenancy, or an added occupant? Did the last original occupant leave?
rows.notes: Owner-supplied, unverified: continuing tenancy from April 1, 2026 at $3,995 per month. How to find it: signed leases, move-in and move-out records, and a Rent Board counselor. Costa-Hawkins and Section 6.14 facts decide this.

rows.label: Unit 1: was a Section 6.14 / Costa-Hawkins notice served on the April 2026 occupant?
rows.notes: Not supplied. How to find it: owner's file. Without it, no unlimited increase is supported.

rows.label: Lease terms: does any lease allow a mid-term increase, and when does its fixed term end?
rows.notes: Not supplied for either unit. How to find it: the signed lease text. A fixed term does not allow a mid-term increase unless the agreement says so.

rows.label: Owner occupancy, in-law unit, accessory dwelling unit, or a second structure on the same lot
rows.notes: Not supplied. How to find it: Planning Property Information Map and permit records. These facts can change coverage and exemptions (Q-19, Q-20).

rows.label: Who holds title: individual, trust, LLC, or corporation?
rows.notes: Owner-supplied, unverified: an individual owner (not a corporation). Recorded title not reviewed. AB 1482's single-family exemption depends on owner type and on written notice to the tenant.

rows.label: Repairs, complaints, inspections or citations in the last 180 days; any tenant petition pending
rows.notes: Not supplied for either unit. How to find it: the owner's repair and complaint records; retaliation review depends on these dates (Civil Code 1942.5).

rows.label: 2026-27 Rent Board Fee: paid, or exempt?
rows.notes: Not supplied. Fee is $59.00 per unit for 2026-27, due March 1, 2027; exemption requests close December 14, 2026. How to find it: Rent Board Portal. Paying the fee does not replace Housing Inventory reporting.

rows.label: Status of proposed File 261020 (10% combined cap on banked and capital-improvement increases)
rows.value: Pending Committee Action; not enacted (Legistar, checked 2026-11-13).
rows.notes: Recheck the Legistar status before any banked calculation or notice. Proposal wording may change.

rows.label: Have any increases been noticed to either unit since the last known rent, and on what dates?
rows.notes: Not supplied. How to find it: owner's notices and proofs of service. Ties to DR-04.

sections.title: B. Decision paths for the increase (choose one path, or a combination, before implementing)

rows.label: Verify first; send no notice yet
rows.value: Complete DR-01 to DR-14 and record each unit's anniversary date and rent history before any notice. Consider owner-side legal advice; a tenant lawyer represents the tenant, not the owner.
rows.notes: Lowest exposure; costs time. Check the banking rule first (DP-D). Awaiting your choice - not implemented.

rows.label: Increase each unit on its own record, at most 1.6%, on its own anniversary date
rows.value: Only for a unit whose DR items are verified and whose license is on file for the effective date. Notice: 30 days (90 days if the increase is more than 10%), with dollar amount, percentage and effective date; +5 days if mailed. Illustration only, if the rent history confirms eligibility: $3,995 x 1.6% = $63.92; $3,150 x 1.6% = $50.40.
rows.notes: Matches the per-unit rules. Raising both units is not required (see DP-C). Keep neutral, dated reasons. Awaiting your choice - not implemented.

rows.label: Same neutral written policy for both units
rows.value: Apply the same written policy to each unit on its own anniversary date (for example 1.6%, the same notice template, and the same license check). No official source requires raising both units.
rows.notes: Helpful when both units are eligible on the same facts. If anniversaries or eligibility differ, forcing identical timing could create errors. Awaiting your choice - not implemented.

rows.label: Defer (bank) the annual increase
rows.value: A skipped increase is banked only if at least 24 full months pass without any increase. Banked amounts are added, not compounded, and do not carry to a new tenant. A banked increase still needs a license when imposed.
rows.notes: No notice is needed to defer. Timing risk: a skipped increase is lost if the 24-month rule is not met. File 261020 could cap later banked increases if enacted (F46). Awaiting your choice - not implemented.

rows.label: Larger increase: banked total, Section 6.14, or a petition
rows.value: Not recommended now. Unit 2 conditional arithmetic only: 13.1% (including 1.6%) if nothing was ever imposed since June 1, 2019. This is not a finding.
rows.notes: Highest legal and challenge risk. Decide only after DR items are verified and a lawyer-style review (section C) is complete. Awaiting your choice - not implemented.

sections.title: C. Lawyer-review criteria: what a San Francisco tenant lawyer will test

rows.label: Coverage is documented from an official record
rows.notes: Not yet done for these units. Record the PIM report and date.

rows.label: Rent Increase License is on file on the effective date
rows.notes: Not yet confirmed. Save the Portal status with the date checked.

rows.label: Base rent, anniversary date and increase history are documented
rows.notes: Not yet documented for either unit. Keep the full ledger.

rows.label: The math is correct: base rent x rate in effect on the increase date; base rent only; no rounding up
rows.value: Rate 1.6% for 3/1/26-2/28/27 (verified); the rate on the increase date governs.
rows.notes: Use the Form 571 table for the rate on the effective date.

rows.label: Notice content and timing: dollar amount, percentage, effective date, banked portion; 30 or 90 days; +5 days if mailed
rows.value: Rules verified on SF.gov; no notice has been drafted or served.
rows.notes: Template and checklist: Notice Checklist and Notice Worksheet pages.

rows.label: Delivery and proof of service follow Civil Code 827 and CCP 1013
rows.value: Rules verified; not yet applied to any notice.
rows.notes: Keep proof of service with the notice.

rows.label: No extra rent for an added occupant; no market-rate reset without verified facts
rows.value: Verified rule: extra rent for a new or added roommate is unlawful. No reset facts are verified for Unit 1.
rows.notes: See Q-14 and Q-09.

rows.label: No retaliation or harassment: review repairs, complaints and the 180-day window
rows.value: Verified rule; the facts for each unit are missing (DR-11).
rows.notes: Check the dates before choosing any path.

rows.label: Non-discrimination: same neutral criteria; no protected characteristic; no unjustified disparate effect
rows.value: Verified legal framework; no discriminatory fact is known, and no lawyer has reviewed any choice.
rows.notes: Document neutral reasons for each unit.

rows.label: The official source check is dated on the day of review, including the status of File 261020
rows.notes: Recheck the day of any notice.

rows.label: Limits of this review
rows.value: Not legal advice. No attorney has approved any increase. Free tenant counseling is for the tenant; the Rent Board counselor does not give legal advice to owners.
rows.notes: Owner-side legal advice is a separate decision (DP-A).
